# Using ISLA {#sec-using}

*Before this chapter:* @sec-isla (what ISLA computes, idea by idea). The
exact forward pass, every argument included, is @sec-architecture; this
chapter refers to it rather than repeating it.

**ISLA ships as one class with one reference configuration, trained and
evaluated by the unified external-aerodynamics recipe, and this chapter is
its operating manual.** It says which configuration to run, how to declare
the boundary conditions, what the model
needs from your data and what it returns, the commands that train and
evaluate it, the one learning rate and why the optimizer matters for it,
how to draw cells at inference, how to load a checkpoint, what a step
costs, and how to check the model's two contracts on your own data. Every
code cell on this page runs on a CPU as the page renders, on the running
airfoil of @sec-problem, with a model far too small to predict anything, so
the shapes and the residuals can be read.

::: {.callout-tip title="If you run one thing"}
From the recipe root, train the DrivAerML Surface model at its reference configuration with
`python src/train.py model=isla_surface dataset=drivaer_ml_surface`, then score it in float32 at 200,000 cells with the
`src/infer.py` command of @sec-using-sampler. Everything else on this page explains what those two commands fix and
how to change them for your data.
:::

```{python}
#| label: setup-using
#| include: false
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from palette import *
import json, inspect, math, os, tempfile, zipfile, warnings
from pathlib import Path
import yaml
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
import torch
import physicsnemo
from physicsnemo.mesh import Mesh
from physicsnemo.experimental.models import ISLA
RES = Path("..") / "results"
RECIPE = Path(physicsnemo.__file__).parent.parent / "examples" / "cfd" / "external_aerodynamics" / "unified_external_aero_recipe"
CONF = RECIPE / "conf" / "model"
DEFAULTS = {k: v.default for k, v in inspect.signature(ISLA.__init__).parameters.items() if v.default is not inspect.Parameter.empty}

def load_cfg(name):
    """A recipe model config with its `defaults` parents merged in (model block and training block)."""
    cfg = yaml.safe_load((CONF / f"{name}.yaml").read_text())
    for parent in cfg.get("defaults", []) or []:
        if isinstance(parent, str):
            base = load_cfg(parent)
            for key in ("model", "training"):
                cfg[key] = {**base.get(key, {}), **cfg.get(key, {})}
            for key in ("compile", "compile_options"):
                cfg.setdefault(key, base.get(key))
    return cfg
def sci(x):
    """3.75e-4 style: the mantissa to the digits it needs, the exponent as an integer."""
    e = int(math.floor(math.log10(abs(x)))); m = x / 10 ** e
    return f"{m:g}e{e}"
ISLA_CFGS = {p.stem: load_cfg(p.stem) for p in sorted(CONF.glob("isla_*.yaml"))}
TRAIN = yaml.safe_load((RECIPE / "conf" / "train.yaml").read_text())
BASE = yaml.safe_load((RECIPE / "conf" / "base.yaml").read_text())
```

## Which configuration {#sec-using-config}

**Run ISLA in its reference configuration, which is the class's defaults:
you declare the fields and the task, and leave the sizes alone.** A surface
model that predicts pressure and wall shear stress under one far-field
direction is

```python
from physicsnemo.experimental.models import ISLA
model = ISLA(
    output_schema={"pressure": {"rank": 0}, "wss": {"rank": 1}},
    boundary_schemas={"vehicle": {}},
    global_schema={"U_inf_dir": {"rank": 1}},
)
```

and an interior model adds `interior=True`, which builds ISLA-DTT; `query_independent=False` builds interacting
ISLA instead.

```{python}
#| label: para-using-config
#| output: asis
lrs = {n: c["training"]["optimizer"]["lr"] for n, c in ISLA_CFGS.items()}
sizes = {(c["model"]["hidden"], c["model"]["n_layers"], c["model"]["n_slices"]) for c in ISLA_CFGS.values()}
assert len(set(lrs.values())) == 1 and sizes == {(DEFAULTS["hidden"], DEFAULTS["n_layers"], DEFAULTS["n_slices"])}
print(f"The reference configuration is width `hidden={DEFAULTS['hidden']}`, `n_layers={DEFAULTS['n_layers']}` slice "
      f"layers and `n_slices={DEFAULTS['n_slices']}` slices, trained at learning rate {sci(next(iter(lrs.values())))} on "
      f"{TRAIN['sampling_resolution']:,} sampled cells per case for {TRAIN['training']['num_epochs']} epochs (DeepJEB++ "
      "trains 40 and AeroZoo 250, @sec-fair-comparison). Every one of "
      f"the recipe's {len(ISLA_CFGS)} ISLA model configurations (`conf/model/isla_*.yaml`) sets these sizes and this rate, "
      "so the commands below need no model overrides (read from the configuration files and the constructor's signature "
      "as the page renders).")
```

It was chosen among ISLA configurations that train in under 80 GiB per GPU,
on the DrivAerML Surface task and on HiLiftAeroML at 510 training cases, by
the selection that also fixed the reference configurations of GeoTransolver
(width 256) and Transolver (width 512, 16 layers). The two datasets named
different winners, and the configuration with the best score over both was
taken; @sec-selection gives the rule, the outcome and every candidate. Everything else
about ISLA is fixed in the class: the frame, the routing, the length unit,
the exact wall geometry of interior prediction points, the law of the
interior task's boundary draw, the geometry kernel's selection.

```{python}
#| label: para-using-arguments
#| output: asis
KINDS = {
    "declarations of your data": ["output_schema", "boundary_schemas", "global_schema", "dim"],
    "the dataset constants of declared scales": ["reynolds", "output_stats"],
    "the task and its interior tokens": ["interior", "boundary_tokens", "query_independent"],
    "capacity and execution": ["hidden", "n_layers", "n_slices", "compile_blocks"],
}
SIG = [k for k in inspect.signature(ISLA.__init__).parameters if k != "self"]
assert sorted(sum(KINDS.values(), [])) == sorted(SIG), (KINDS, SIG)
assert all(p.kind is inspect.Parameter.KEYWORD_ONLY for k, p in inspect.signature(ISLA.__init__).parameters.items() if k != "self")
REQUIRED = [k for k in SIG if inspect.signature(ISLA.__init__).parameters[k].default is inspect.Parameter.empty]
print(f"The constructor's {len(SIG)} arguments (@tbl-arch-switches), all keyword-only, are of {['no', 'one', 'two', 'three', 'four', 'five'][len(KINDS)]} kinds: "
      + "; ".join(f"{kind} ({', '.join(f'`{a}`' for a in args)})" for kind, args in KINDS.items())
      + f". Only {' and '.join(f'`{a}`' for a in REQUIRED)} have no default (read from the constructor's signature as the "
      "page renders). A change of size is an experiment, not a configuration of the book; the capacity studies of "
      "@sec-capacity are where such changes are measured.")
```

::: {.callout-note title="Interacting or read-only prediction points"}
ISLA's default interior form is ISLA-DTT (`query_independent=True`), whose
read-only prediction points never write into the slices and read the
boundary cells through a Barnes–Hut forest (@sec-arch-passive-decoder). Its
prediction at a point depends on that point and the boundary alone, so it
answers at an arbitrary point set, one point at a time or in chunks
(@sec-aerozoo-form). An interior prediction of interacting ISLA
(`query_independent=False`) is a function of the whole set of prediction
points, because those points are interacting tokens: they carry routing
mass and help form the slices (@sec-arch-modes). Deploy interacting ISLA at
its training point count and state that count with every interior number.

```{python}
#| label: para-using-query-population
#| output: asis
import records as R
from physicsnemo.experimental.models.isla.tree_read import TREE_READ_THETA
QP = R.load("probes090", "results/qpop/reduced.json")
QV = [QP[f"r090_vol_isla_seed{s}"]["ratio_to_native_h"] for s in (42, 43)]
qv = lambda mode: [sum(v[mode][f] for v in QV) / len(QV) for f in ("pressure_l2", "velocity_l2")]
QD = R.load("probes090", "results/qpop_afeag/reduced.json")
qd = max(abs(x - 1) for s in (42, 43) for mode in QD[f"r090eag_af_dtt_seed{s}"]["ratio_to_native_h"].values() for x in mode.values())
print(f"On the DrivAerML Volume task, the standing's interacting ISLA asked for its scored points in four "
      f"chunks moves its pressure and velocity error by at most {100 * (max(qv('chunks4')) - 1):.1f}%, but 1,000 of those points "
      f"asked for on their own raise it {min(qv('sub1000')):.1f} to {max(qv('sub1000')):.1f} times, and points asked for one at a "
      f"time {min(qv('sub1')):.0f} to {max(qv('sub1')):.0f} times (seed means). On AirfRANS, ISLA-DTT's error moves by at most "
      f"{sci(float(f'{qd:.1g}'))} relative under every such change of the request, float32 roundoff (the AirfRANS standing's checkpoints, "
      f"trained without compilation). Its tree read is a Barnes–Hut approximation at opening angle $\\theta = "
      f"{TREE_READ_THETA:g}$, whose error vanishes as $\\theta \\to 0$. Data: {R.source('probes090', 'results/qpop/reduced.json')}; {R.source('probes090', 'results/qpop_afeag/reduced.json')}.")
# DEFAULT-DTT's query-independence check on the class as it is: one real case per interior dataset, fresh weights, eager,
# evaluation mode; the largest change at the shared points when 1,000 other points join the request, over the field's largest value
import standing as S
QI = R.md_table("default_dtt", "FINAL_REPORT.md", index=1)
qi = lambda col: (min(float(r[col]) for r in QI), max(float(r[col]) for r in QI))
qd64, qi64 = qi("QI fp64, DTT"), qi("QI fp64, ISLA")
assert "1,000 other points are added" in " ".join(R.load("default_dtt", "FINAL_REPORT.md").split())
print()
print(f"With freshly initialized weights, on one real case of each of the {S._COUNT[len(QI)]} interior datasets, "
      "eager and in evaluation mode, adding 1,000 other points to a request moves ISLA-DTT's outputs at the shared points by "
      f"{sci(qd64[0])} to {sci(qd64[1])} of the field's largest value in float64, roundoff, and interacting ISLA's by "
      f"{sci(qi64[0])} to {sci(qi64[1])}. Data: {R.source('default_dtt', 'FINAL_REPORT.md')} (per interior dataset).")
```

What the two forms measure on the same datasets is in
@sec-interior-read-only, @sec-airfrans-read-only and @sec-aerozoo-form.
:::

## What the model needs from your data {#sec-using-inputs}

**ISLA takes the boundary as one mesh per named boundary condition, the
prediction points as a point cloud, and the problem's data as named fields
of declared rank; it returns a point cloud with the outputs in its point
data. The inputs that are easy to get wrong are the measures, which must be
proportional to the measure each cell represents, with one constant across
every boundary mesh, the orientation of the cells, and the global
directions, which must be directions.**
The forward call is keyword-only and takes four arguments, of which a
task passes three:

- `boundary_meshes`: a mapping from the boundary-condition names declared
  in `boundary_schemas` to `Mesh[dim - 1, dim]` objects, a triangulated
  surface in three dimensions or a polyline in two. A boundary cell has its
  centroid as position, its normal as normal, and its effective measure
  (`cell_data["_effective_measure"]` when present, else the geometric
  measure) as measure weight. Any non-empty subset of the declared names may
  be passed, in any order: the model reads the given conditions in sorted
  name order, so two orders of the mapping give bitwise the same output, and
  a condition left out contributes nothing, as one with zero cells does. A
  name that is not declared is an error. Each mesh's `cell_data` carries its
  own condition's declared fields, read by name; other cell data are
  ignored. On the surface task every cell of every given mesh is a token,
  those of the boundaries it predicts at and those read as conditions only
  (a wind tunnel's floor, walls, inlet and outlet). On the interior task
  every mesh goes in at full resolution: its cells are the surface the
  prediction points' geometry is measured against, and the model draws its
  boundary tokens from them (@sec-using-interior).
- `prediction_points`: for the interior task, a point-cloud `Mesh`, of
  which only the `points` are read, or a bare `(Q, dim)` tensor. A
  prediction point carries no declared field: its position, and the
  geometry the model computes for it, are all it has. Omitted on a surface
  task.
- `prediction_boundaries`: for the surface task, and required there, a
  non-empty list of distinct names of given boundaries, at whose cells the
  outputs are predicted (DrivAerML Surface: `["vehicle"]`, the tunnel's
  four pieces read as conditions only). Their order does not matter, and
  the argument owns no parameters: the head reads the same tokens whichever
  boundaries carry the outputs, and only the rows it returns differ.
  Omitted on an interior task, which refuses it.
- `global_data`: a TensorDict or a mapping with the `global_schema` fields
  as leaves, a `(dim,)` vector for a rank-1 field and a scalar for a rank-0
  field. Extra leaves are ignored; a missing one is an error.

Each declaration, `output_schema`, each condition's schema in
`boundary_schemas`, and `global_schema`, maps a field name to a *rank spec*:
`{"rank": r}`, with `"symmetric": True` for a symmetric tensor of rank 2 or
more and `"parity": "odd"` for a pseudotensor output (a vorticity). Rank 0
is a scalar, rank 1 a vector, rank 2 a matrix that rotates as a tensor.
Inputs go up to rank 2 and outputs up to rank 4. Global inputs are rank 0
or 1. One name declares one field, so a parameter vector is several rank-0
names.

The example below builds the airfoil as a polyline `Mesh`, orients its
cells so that their normals point out of the body into the fluid, and calls
a surface model and an interior model on it, each with one boundary
condition, `airfoil`, that declares no field.

```{python}
#| label: using-forward-demo
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
J = joukowski(n_cells=80)                                # the book's running example
verts = torch.as_tensor(J["xy"], dtype=torch.float64)    # (81, 2) closed polyline
cells = torch.stack([torch.arange(80), torch.arange(1, 81)], dim=1)   # (80, 2)
airfoil = Mesh(points=verts, cells=cells)                # Mesh[1, 2]: a polyline
# A cell's normal follows its vertex order; ISLA reads it as given: orient the cells into the fluid.
if ((airfoil.cell_centroids - verts.mean(0)) * airfoil.cell_normals).sum(-1).mean() < 0:
    cells = cells.flip(1)
    airfoil = Mesh(points=verts, cells=cells)
freestream = torch.tensor([1.0, 0.1], dtype=torch.float64)  # a rank-1 global input

torch.manual_seed(0)
surface = ISLA(output_schema={"cp": {"rank": 0}, "tau": {"rank": 1}}, boundary_schemas={"airfoil": {}},
               global_schema={"freestream": {"rank": 1}},
               hidden=32, n_layers=2, n_slices=8, dim=2).double().eval()
with torch.no_grad():
    out = surface(boundary_meshes={"airfoil": airfoil}, prediction_boundaries=["airfoil"], global_data={"freestream": freestream})

interior = ISLA(output_schema={"p": {"rank": 0}, "u": {"rank": 1}}, boundary_schemas={"airfoil": {}},
                global_schema={"freestream": {"rank": 1}}, interior=True,
                hidden=32, n_layers=2, n_slices=8, dim=2).double().eval()
xs = torch.linspace(-1.5, 2.5, 40, dtype=torch.float64)
ys = torch.linspace(-1.5, 1.5, 30, dtype=torch.float64)
grid = torch.stack(torch.meshgrid(xs, ys, indexing="ij"), -1).reshape(-1, 2)  # (1200, 2)
with torch.no_grad():
    field = interior(boundary_meshes={"airfoil": airfoil}, prediction_points=grid,
                     global_data={"freestream": freestream})
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-using-shapes
#| output: asis
shp = lambda t: str(tuple(t.shape))
rows = [
    ("input", "`airfoil.points`", shp(airfoil.points), "polyline vertices"),
    ("input", "`airfoil.cells`", shp(airfoil.cells), "segments, by vertex index"),
    ("read by the model", "`airfoil.cell_centroids`", shp(airfoil.cell_centroids), "token positions $x_i$"),
    ("read by the model", "`airfoil.cell_normals`", shp(airfoil.cell_normals), "outward unit normals $n_i$"),
    ("read by the model", "`airfoil.cell_areas`", shp(airfoil.cell_areas), "measure weights $w_i$ (segment lengths)"),
    ("input", "`global_data[\"freestream\"]`", shp(freestream), "the global direction $g_1$"),
    ("input", "`prediction_points` (interior)", shp(grid), "the prediction points $x_q$"),
    ("output, surface", "`out.points`", shp(out.points), "the prediction boundary's cell centroids"),
    ("output, surface", "`out.point_data[\"cp\"]`", shp(out.point_data["cp"]), "rank 0"),
    ("output, surface", "`out.point_data[\"tau\"]`", shp(out.point_data["tau"]), "rank 1"),
    ("output, interior", "`field.points`", shp(field.points), "the prediction points"),
    ("output, interior", "`field.point_data[\"p\"]`", shp(field.point_data["p"]), "rank 0"),
    ("output, interior", "`field.point_data[\"u\"]`", shp(field.point_data["u"]), "rank 1"),
]
o = "| | tensor | shape | meaning |\n|:----|:------|:--|:------|\n" + "".join(f"| {a} | {b} | {c} | {d} |\n" for a, b, c, d in rows)
print(o)
print(": What goes in and what comes out of the example above, read from the tensors as the page renders. How to read this: "
      "a rank-$r$ output has $r$ trailing axes of size `dim`; the surface outputs are at the prediction boundaries' cells in token order, the "
      "interior outputs at the prediction points in request order. The model's outputs here are untrained.")
```

The output is a point-cloud `Mesh`. On the surface task its `points` are
the centroids of the prediction boundaries' cells, those boundaries in
sorted name order and each one's cells in its mesh's order; on the interior
task they are the prediction points. Its `point_data` holds one leaf per declared output
at its natural shape, and its `global_data` is the selected `global_data`
passed through.

### Boundary conditions by name {#sec-using-conditions}

**Declare each boundary condition by name with the fields it prescribes;
the condition's identity is in the model's parameters, so no tag field
names it.** `boundary_schemas` maps each name to its schema: an inlet's
prescribed velocity as `{"bc_velocity": {"rank": 1}}`, a loaded face's
pressure as `{"bc_pressure": {"rank": 0}}`, a no-slip wall as `{}`. The
constructor stores the names sorted, as `model.boundary_names`. A name is a
non-empty string without `"."`, and it may not be an attribute of
`nn.ModuleDict` (`keys`, `update`, `training`, ...), because the names key
the `ModuleDict` that holds the conditions' parameters; either fault is a
`ValueError` at construction.

Each condition owns an input layer, `boundary_conditions[name].seed`, a
linear map without bias from the condition's seed (a constant 1, the
cosines $n_i \cdot \hat g_k$, the invariants of its own fields and the
global scalars) to the token width, followed by the shared GELU and linear
layer `embed`. Its column on the constant is the condition's learned
offset, so two conditions that declare no field still start apart and stay
apart. A condition's vector and tensor fields reach the slice layers
through its own linear maps (`vector_map`, `tensor_map`) onto shared
channels, as many as the widest condition has; the slice layers themselves
are shared by every condition (@sec-arch-seed). The cell below declares two
conditions on the airfoil, a blowing slot near the trailing edge with a
prescribed jet velocity and the rest of the wall, and calls the model with
the conditions in both orders, with one of them alone, and with two names
it does not accept.

```{python}
#| label: using-conditions-demo
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
c = airfoil.cell_centroids
slot = (c[:, 1] > 0) & (c[:, 0] > c[:, 0].quantile(0.8))      # upper surface, last fifth of the chord
n_jet = 0.3 * airfoil.cell_normals[slot]                      # blowing along the normal, into the fluid
jet = Mesh(points=verts, cells=cells[slot], cell_data={"u_jet": n_jet})
wall = Mesh(points=verts, cells=cells[~slot])

torch.manual_seed(0)
two = ISLA(output_schema={"cp": {"rank": 0}, "tau": {"rank": 1}},
           boundary_schemas={"wall": {}, "jet": {"u_jet": {"rank": 1}}},
           global_schema={"freestream": {"rank": 1}},
           hidden=32, n_layers=2, n_slices=8, dim=2).double().eval()
g = {"freestream": freestream}
with torch.no_grad():
    a = two(boundary_meshes={"wall": wall, "jet": jet}, prediction_boundaries=["jet", "wall"], global_data=g)
    b = two(boundary_meshes={"jet": jet, "wall": wall}, prediction_boundaries=["jet", "wall"], global_data=g)
    alone = two(boundary_meshes={"wall": wall}, prediction_boundaries=["wall"], global_data=g)
# One Mesh at the prediction boundaries' cells, sorted by name: split it per condition.
counts = [{"jet": jet, "wall": wall}[name].n_cells for name in two.boundary_names]
cp_by_condition = dict(zip(two.boundary_names, torch.split(a.point_data["cp"], counts)))

refused = {}
for label, call in {
    "an nn.ModuleDict attribute as a name": lambda: ISLA(output_schema={"cp": {"rank": 0}}, boundary_schemas={"keys": {}}, dim=2),
    "an undeclared name in forward": lambda: two(boundary_meshes={"flap": wall}, prediction_boundaries=["flap"], global_data=g),
}.items():
    try:
        call()
    except ValueError as err:
        refused[label] = str(err)
```

```{python}
#| label: para-using-conditions
#| output: asis
same = all(torch.equal(a.point_data[k], b.point_data[k]) for k in ("cp", "tau")) and torch.equal(a.points, b.points)
print(f"`two.boundary_names` is {two.boundary_names}: declared as `wall`, `jet`, stored sorted. The slot has {jet.n_cells} "
      f"cells and the wall {wall.n_cells}; the output has {a.n_points} points, the slot's first. The two orders of the mapping give "
      f"{'bitwise equal' if same else 'different'} outputs, and the wall alone gives {alone.n_points} points, a prediction "
      "for a case without the slot. `torch.split` by the conditions' cell counts, in `boundary_names` order, gives each "
      f"condition its own rows ({', '.join(f'`{k}`: {tuple(v.shape)}' for k, v in cp_by_condition.items())}). Both "
      "conditions carry outputs here, so both are named in `prediction_boundaries`; a task whose outputs live on one "
      "boundary names that one, and the others are read as conditions only. The two refused calls raise `ValueError`:")
print()
for label, msg in refused.items():
    print(f"- {label}: \"{msg}\"")
print()
assert len(refused) == 2 and same
```

**The surface output is one `Mesh`, not one per condition.** The recipe's
loss, metrics and inference consume one set of targets over points, and the
interior task's prediction points belong to no condition, so a mapping of
meshes would only move the concatenation into the recipe. Where the
dataset's scored points are in another order, the recipe puts them in the
prediction order (`reorder_interior`, @sec-using-recipe-conditions).

Four of the inputs need a word.

**The measures must be proportional to what each cell represents.** A
common factor is invisible. The routing reads $\log w$ through a softmax,
which a common shift does not move; the routing mass of interacting ISLA's
$Q$ prediction points (ISLA-DTT's carry none), $\omega + \log \sum_i w_i - \log Q$
with a learned $\omega$ (@sec-arch-modes), shifts by the same constant; and scaling every
measure by 5 leaves every output unchanged
(@tbl-using-contracts). What the model reads is each cell's share of the
boundary, so one constant must hold across all the boundary meshes of a
case. A surface model reads every cell it is given, so when the recipe
keeps $n$ of $N$ surface cells, each kept cell carries the
Horvitz–Thompson weight, its area divided by its probability of being kept
($N/n$ times its area under a uniform draw), in the mesh's
`_effective_measure` cell field. That weight is an importance weight: the
measure-weighted sums the routing takes are then unbiased estimates of
integrals over the whole surface, not over the retained fraction of it
(@sec-isla-quadrature). Under a uniform draw at one rate the factor $N/n$
is common to every cell; it matters where the probability of being kept
differs between cells or between meshes. A boundary passed
whole, like the airfoil above, needs no such field, and an interior model,
which takes its boundary whole and draws its own tokens, computes the
weights itself (@sec-using-interior). Measures carry their
represented dimension and scale geometrically: on a planar problem the
measure is the segment length.

```{python}
#| label: para-using-ht
#| output: asis
torch.manual_seed(1)
keep = torch.randperm(airfoil.n_cells)[:40]
kept = Mesh(points=verts, cells=cells[keep], cell_data={"_effective_measure": airfoil.cell_areas[keep] * airfoil.n_cells / 40})
print(f"On the airfoil: its {airfoil.n_cells} segments have total length {airfoil.cell_areas.sum():.4f}. A uniform draw of 40 "
      f"of them has raw lengths summing to {airfoil.cell_areas[keep].sum():.4f}, about half; with the factor "
      f"{airfoil.n_cells}/40 their effective measures sum to {kept.cell_data['_effective_measure'].sum():.4f}, the whole "
      "airfoil to sampling error.")
```

**A rank-1 global input is a direction.** The model normalizes each global
direction and discards its magnitude. For external aerodynamics the
recipe's `ComputeFreestreamDirection` writes the unit far-field direction
`U_inf_dir` from the solver's velocity (@sec-unit-direction-rule).
GeoTransolver and Transolver do not apply this rule; what they read on each
dataset is in @tbl-model-inputs.

**A global direction must be a datum of the problem.** The inlet direction,
a load direction and gravity are admissible. The axes of the dataset's
coordinate frame are not: they describe how the cases were posed, not the
PDE, and a solver never takes them (@sec-pose-prior). Ground planes and
symmetry planes are real boundaries and belong among the boundary meshes.

**A magnitude that matters is a rank-0 global input, or a declared scale.**
Declare it as a rank-0 field and pass it under its name, and the model
learns its effect as it learns any other parameter: no fixed power of a
far-field speed is a physical law for every output (a pressure coefficient
is of degree zero in it, a dimensional pressure of degree two). Where the
units of the fields are known, declare them instead, and the model makes
its inputs and outputs dimensionless by the case's own scales
(@sec-using-scales). The AirfRANS configuration takes the inlet speed that
way, as the magnitude of its velocity source `U_inf` (@tbl-using-configs
lists every configuration's global inputs, @tbl-airfrans-inputs AirfRANS's
whole input).

### Declared scales {#sec-using-scales}

**A model can bring its own scales: each field declares its units, and ISLA
divides the inputs and multiplies the outputs by scales it computes from
each case.** The declarations are opt-in keys beside a field's `rank`, on a
condition's schema, on `global_schema` and on `output_schema`. `units` gives
the field's exponents of three base scales: the length unit $L$, a velocity
$U$ and a density $\rho$ (`{U: 2, rho: 1}` for a gauge pressure). `scale`
gives a positive constant $c$, the typical size of the field once it is
dimensionless. The model computes the scales of each case in float64, from
the full-resolution boundary and the global inputs, before the token draw:

- **Length.** $L$ is the length unit of every model (@sec-arch-frame).
- **Velocity.** A field flagged `velocity_scale: true` is a *source*: one or
  more rank-1 boundary fields, or one rank-1 global. Over the boundary
  sources' cells with measures $a$, $U \equiv (\sum a \lvert v \rvert^2 /
  \sum a)^{1/2}$, and the direction $\hat g \equiv \sum a v / \lvert
  \sum a v \rvert$ is appended to the global directions. A global source
  gives $U = \lvert v \rvert$ and is a global direction already.
- **Density and viscosity.** A rank-0 global with the `role` `density` is
  $\rho$; one with the `role` `viscosity` is $\nu$. Both are consumed, not
  read as scalars. With a viscosity the model appends one global scalar,
  $\log_{10} \mathrm{Re}$ with $\mathrm{Re} \equiv U L / \nu$, minus a mean and
  divided by a standard deviation that the constructor's
  `reynolds={"mean": ..., "std": ...}` gives.

Each declared input enters divided by $c \prod_k \text{scale}_k^{e_k}$, its
constant times its units' scales, and each declared output is the head's
dimensionless prediction $\hat y$ times the same product, $y = c\, \hat y
\prod_k \text{scale}_k^{e_k}$, assembled in the parameters' precision
(float32) even under autocast, and then
standardized by the dataset's constant `output_stats`, so the model returns
the standardized targets the loss compares. A model that declares nothing is
the unscaled model. A similarity of the problem (lengths times one factor,
velocities another, densities a third) leaves every internal state unchanged
and scales each output by its units, a contract the tests check in float64
(`test_isla_scales.py`).

```{python}
#| label: para-using-scales
#| output: asis
import standing as S
_scaled = [n for n in ISLA_CFGS if ISLA(**{k: v for k, v in S.recipe_model(n).items() if k in ("output_schema", "boundary_schemas",
           "global_schema", "reynolds", "interior", "dim")}, hidden=8, n_layers=1, n_slices=2)._scaled]
_az = S.isla_constants("isla_volume_aerozoo"); _af = S.isla_constants("isla_volume_airfrans")
_fit = json.load(open(RES / "aerozoo_dataset" / "isla_constants_fits.json"))["fits"]["full"]["scale_quartiles"]
_e = lambda x: sci(float(f"{x:.2g}"))   # 4.7e-4
_orders = [abs(math.log10(c)) for c in (_az["output_scale"]["nut"], _az["output_scale"]["omega"], _af["output_scale"]["nut"])]
print(f"**The constant $c$ starts the head at the right size.** A freshly initialized head predicts values of order one. "
      f"Made dimensionless by $U L$, an eddy viscosity is far smaller: on AeroZoo's training cases the per-case RMS of "
      f"$\\nu_t / (U L)$ has the median {_e(_az['output_scale']['nut'])} (quartiles {_e(_fit['nut'][0])} and {_e(_fit['nut'][2])}), "
      f"and that of $\\omega L / U$ the median {_az['output_scale']['omega']:,.0f} (quartiles {_fit['omega'][0]:,.0f} and "
      f"{_fit['omega'][2]:,.0f}); on AirfRANS's, whose length unit the far field sets, $\\nu_t / (U L)$ has the median "
      f"{_e(_af['output_scale']['nut'])}. Without $c$ the "
      f"head would start {min(_orders):.0f} to {max(_orders):.0f} orders of magnitude off on these fields; with it, each starts at "
      "order one and learns the spread around the median.")
print()
print(f"These constants, the two of `reynolds` and every $c$, belong to a split of a dataset: each is fitted on the split's training cases "
      f"(the medians of per-case RMS values, and the mean and standard deviation of $\\log_{{10}}(U L / \\nu)$, through the class's "
      f"own scale functions), and each dataset file holds its split's values under `isla_constants`. The model configurations "
      f"leave them `null`, and the recipe's `train.py` and `infer.py` fill them from the dataset file; a configuration whose "
      f"dataset file lacks one is refused. Of the recipe's {len(ISLA_CFGS)} ISLA configurations, "
      f"{' and '.join(f'`{n}`' for n in _scaled)} declare scales (@sec-data-aerozoo, @sec-data-airfrans); the others declare none, "
      "so for them the scales change nothing. Source: the recipe's `conf/model/isla_*.yaml` and `datasets/*.yaml`, and "
      "results/aerozoo_dataset/isla_constants_fits.json for the quartiles.")
```

### The interior task: exact geometry and the in-model draw {#sec-using-interior}

**On the interior task, pass every boundary at full resolution and the
prediction points as bare positions: the model computes each point's
geometry exactly from the whole surface and draws its own boundary tokens.**
For each prediction point $x_q$ the model finds the closest point $p_q$ on
the union of the given meshes' cells (point to face, a search of the
model's own tree over the cells in three dimensions and a brute force over
the segments in two). The signed distance $d_q = \pm|x_q - p_q|$ takes the
sign of the generalized winding number of the oriented cells, positive on
the side the normals point to; the direction $u_q$ is the cell's normal
turned toward the query when $p_q$ lies inside a cell, the least-norm point
of the tied features' directions where several features tie, else
$(x_q - p_q)/|x_q - p_q|$. The point reads $s_q = d_q / L$, in the length unit $L$ (@sec-arch-frame), and
$\operatorname{asinh}(s_q / 10^{-6})$ as its two distance channels and
$\hat\nu_q = \operatorname{sign}(d_q)\, u_q$, with $\operatorname{sign}(0) =
+1$, as its direction (@sec-arch-interior-geometry). Both are continuous
through the surface, the same for every draw of the boundary tokens,
unchanged when a cell is split, and convergent as $O(h^2)$ under refinement,
like a stored signed-distance field computed from the same surface. The
model therefore reads no stored field and takes no per-point input at all,
as Peter's boundary-only input ruling has it: "just pass in the
full-resolution boundary surfaces and ONLY that". The datasets compute `sdf` and `sdf_normals` for the baselines, whose
inputs they are.

The boundary tokens are a sample of the same cells, drawn inside the
forward pass (`sampling.sample_boundary_cells`):

- **Budget.** `boundary_tokens` (default 200,000) tokens per case in
  total, shared over the given conditions by water filling: equal shares, a
  condition with fewer cells than its share kept whole and its unused share
  given to the others. The count is exactly $\min(\text{cells},
  \texttt{boundary\_tokens})$, a function of the cell counts alone, so the
  draw has static shapes and compiles into the whole-model graph; under the
  per-block compile it runs eagerly, outside the compiled slice blocks.
- **Law.** A cell is kept with probability $\pi_i$ proportional to its
  measure, capped at one, by systematic sampling along the Morton order of
  the centroids in the boundary's canonical frame, computed in float64: one start $u$, then every unit step along the cells laid end
  to end, each as an interval of length $\pi_i$. The sample is spread over
  the surface rather than clumped.
- **Weights.** Each kept cell carries its Horvitz–Thompson measure $a_i /
  \pi_i$, so every measure-weighted sum over the tokens is an unbiased
  quadrature of the full surface, exact on a condition kept whole.
- **Start.** In training $u$ is uniform from the global torch RNG, a new
  quadrature of the same surface at every step (`torch.manual_seed`
  reproduces a run); in evaluation (`model.eval()`) $u = 0.5$
  (`EVAL_START` in `model.py`), so inference is deterministic.

A surface model reads every cell it is given and samples none: it predicts
at the cells of its prediction boundaries, and its constructor raises a
`ValueError` for any
`boundary_tokens` other than the default. The cell below draws 40 tokens from the
airfoil's 80 segments with an interior model.

```{python}
#| label: using-draw-demo
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
from physicsnemo.experimental.models.isla import model as isla_model
from physicsnemo.experimental.models.isla.sampling import sample_boundary_cells

lengths = airfoil.cell_areas
kept, w_ht = sample_boundary_cells([lengths], [airfoil.cell_centroids], 40,
                                   torch.tensor(isla_model.EVAL_START, dtype=torch.float64))

torch.manual_seed(0)
sparse = ISLA(output_schema={"p": {"rank": 0}}, boundary_schemas={"airfoil": {}},
              global_schema={"freestream": {"rank": 1}}, interior=True, boundary_tokens=40,
              hidden=32, n_layers=2, n_slices=8, dim=2).double()
ask = dict(boundary_meshes={"airfoil": airfoil}, prediction_points=grid, global_data={"freestream": freestream})
with torch.no_grad():
    sparse.eval();  ev1, ev2 = sparse(**ask).point_data["p"], sparse(**ask).point_data["p"]
    sparse.train(); tr1, tr2 = sparse(**ask).point_data["p"], sparse(**ask).point_data["p"]
```

```{python}
#| label: para-using-draw
#| output: asis
print(f"The draw keeps {kept.numel()} of the {airfoil.n_cells} segments. Their raw lengths sum to "
      f"{lengths[kept].sum():.4f} and their Horvitz–Thompson measures to {w_ht.sum():.4f}, against the airfoil's "
      f"{lengths.sum():.4f}. Two evaluation-mode calls give "
      f"{'bitwise equal' if torch.equal(ev1, ev2) else 'different'} predictions; two training-mode calls draw two "
      f"samples, and their predictions differ by {float((tr1 - tr2).norm() / tr2.norm()):.1e} "
      "in relative L2 on this untrained model.")
```

### Orientation {#sec-using-orientation}

**Orient every boundary so that its normals point into the domain where
the prediction points lie: into the fluid for a flow, into the solid for a
stress problem.** The model reads each cell's normal as given and never
flips it. On the interior task the normals sign the distance, so a model
trained with normals into the fluid sees positive distances at all its
prediction points and directions $\hat\nu_q$ pointing away from the wall. A
boundary wound the other way presents negative distances and reversed
normals to every invariant: a different input, not a symmetry the model
undoes. The model cannot choose the orientation itself, because a mesh
does not say which side is the domain (an inlet, an open wall or a duct has
no inside), and the winding-number sign assumes consistently oriented
cells: it is positive on the side their normals point to. On the surface task the orientation enters only through
the normals' invariants and needs only to be the same across a dataset's
cases.

The recipe sets the orientation per dataset file with the transform
`FlipBoundaryOrientation` (`src/domain_transforms.py`): for each boundary
it names, it swaps the last two vertices of every cell, which reverses the
normal and leaves the cell and its measure unchanged, and negates any
stored normal fields it lists, so the stored files stay as they are.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-using-orientation
#| output: asis
DSETS = RECIPE / "datasets"
def flips(path):
    """The boundaries a dataset file's FlipBoundaryOrientation steps reverse (none: the empty list)."""
    steps = (yaml.safe_load(path.read_text()).get("pipeline") or {}).get("transforms") or []
    return [b for t in steps if "FlipBoundaryOrientation" in str(t.get("_target_", "")) for b in t["boundaries"]]
families = {"DrivAerML Volume (`drivaer_ml_volume_reference*`)": "drivaer_ml_volume_reference*.yaml",
            "AeroZoo (`aerozoo_volume*`, `aerozoo_uvolume*`)": "aerozoo_*volume*.yaml",
            "AirfRANS interior (`airfrans_*volume*`)": "airfrans_*volume*.yaml",
            "DrivAerML Surface (`drivaer_ml_surface*`)": "drivaer_ml_surface*.yaml"}
o = "| dataset files | files | boundaries reversed |\n|---|--:|---|\n"
FLIPS = {}
for fam, pat in families.items():
    FLIPS[pat] = found = {tuple(flips(p)) for p in sorted(DSETS.glob(pat))}
    n = len(list(DSETS.glob(pat)))
    o += f"| {fam} | {n} | " + ("; ".join(", ".join(f"`{b}`" for b in f) or "none" for f in sorted(found))) + " |\n"
assert FLIPS["drivaer_ml_volume_reference*.yaml"] == {("vehicle",)}, FLIPS
assert FLIPS["aerozoo_*volume*.yaml"] == {("inlet", "outlet", "no_slip", "slip")}, FLIPS
assert FLIPS["airfrans_*volume*.yaml"] == {()} and FLIPS["drivaer_ml_surface*.yaml"] == {()}, FLIPS
print(o)
print(": The boundaries the recipe's dataset files reverse with `FlipBoundaryOrientation`, read from `datasets/*.yaml` as the "
      "page renders. How to read this: the DrivAerML vehicle is stored wound into the body and AeroZoo's four boundaries out of "
      "the fluid (the OpenFOAM convention), so both are reversed; AeroZoo reverses them after the passes that compute "
      "GeoTransolver's stored distances, which are those of the stored files. AirfRANS's airfoil is stored with its normals "
      "into the fluid and is read as it is. A surface task reads no distance. The table does not cover the solid-mechanics "
      "datasets, whose files are not in the recipe tree (see below).")
```

Of the solids, the Tensile2d specimen's polyline is stored with its normals
into the specimen and needs no reversal (`isla_tensile2d.yaml`). The lug's
surface triangles are stored wound out of the solid, so `isla_lug.yaml`
is paired with a dataset file that reverses `surface` before the split into
conditions.

### The recipe's contract and the configurations {#sec-using-recipe-conditions}

**A recipe configuration names each boundary condition twice, once in
`model.boundary_schemas` with its fields and once in
`forward_kwargs.boundary_meshes` with the datapipe boundary it is read
from.** A recipe model configuration declares `input_type: mesh` and
`output_type: mesh`. Under the first, the datapipe's `Mesh` objects and
per-case tensors pass to `forward` as they are, one case per step with no
batch axis, through a `forward_kwargs` mapping whose keys are the
argument names above and whose values name the datapipe fields (one
`boundaries.<name>` per condition under `boundary_meshes`, the interior
point cloud under `prediction_points`, the case's global tensors under
`global_data`); a surface configuration gives its prediction boundaries
as a literal list of names (`prediction_boundaries: {literal: [vehicle]}`). Under the second, the recipe reads its targets out of the
returned mesh's `point_data` by the names of the `output_schema`
declaration. GLOBE, another surrogate the recipe trains
(`conf/model/globe_surface.yaml`), uses the same contract, so the two models
are swapped by changing the model block alone.

Each configuration reads every piece of the domain's boundary its dataset
stores, by name, and the configurations fall into three families. On
DrivAerML, AirfRANS and HiLiftAeroML no condition declares a field: the
DrivAerML configurations read the vehicle and the four other pieces of the
wind tunnel's box (`no_slip`, the ground under and behind the car; `slip`,
the sides, the roof and the ground upstream; `inlet`; `outlet`), the
AirfRANS one the airfoil and the far field `freestream`, and the HiLiftAeroML one the wing, the only piece all but two of its files
store. AeroZoo's
four boundaries are four conditions read directly from the dataset, each
declaring only the values it prescribes. The GINOT bracket lug, PLAID
Tensile2d and DeepJEB++ store their conditions in one labelled boundary,
which the ISLA configuration splits into one boundary per condition with the
recipe transform `SplitBoundaryByLabels`, listed under
`dataset_append_transforms`. The recipe appends those steps to the
dataset's own chain for that model configuration only (`src/datasets.py`),
so the baselines read the dataset unchanged. It raises an error for a
configuration whose `boundary_meshes` does not pass every split boundary under its own
name, since a boundary left out would drop its cells without an error. The
split gives each label field's cells to the first condition in `labels`
that marks them and the cells no label marks to `rest`; the source boundary
stays as it is for the baselines.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-using-conditions
#| output: asis
def fields(s):
    return ", ".join(f"`{k}` ({v['rank']})" for k, v in (s or {}).items()) or "none"
o = "| configuration | condition (declared fields, rank) | read from | split of the labelled boundary |\n|---|---|---|---|\n"
for n, c in ISLA_CFGS.items():
    schemas = c["model"]["boundary_schemas"]; given = c["forward_kwargs"]["boundary_meshes"]
    assert set(schemas) == set(given), (n, schemas, given)
    split = [t for t in c.get("dataset_append_transforms") or [] if "SplitBoundaryByLabels" in str(t["_target_"])]
    how = "; ".join(f"`{t['boundary']}` by labels, first wins: " + ", ".join(f"`{k}` ← `{v}`" for k, v in t["labels"].items())
                    + f"; rest `{t['rest']}`" + ("; scored points reordered (`reorder_interior`)" if t.get("reorder_interior") else "")
                    for t in split) or "none"
    for i, name in enumerate(sorted(schemas)):
        o += (f"| {'`' + n + '`' if i == 0 else ''} | `{name}` ({fields(schemas[name])}) | `{given[name]}` | "
              f"{how if i == 0 else ''} |\n")
print(o)
PB = {n: c["forward_kwargs"]["prediction_boundaries"]["literal"] for n, c in ISLA_CFGS.items() if "prediction_boundaries" in c["forward_kwargs"]}
assert set(PB) == {n for n, c in ISLA_CFGS.items() if not c["model"].get("interior")}, PB
print(": The boundary conditions of every ISLA configuration of the recipe, in the model's sorted order, with the datapipe "
      "boundary each is read from and the split that makes it (`conf/model/isla_*.yaml`, read as the page renders). The surface "
      "configurations predict at " + "; ".join(f"`{n}`: " + ", ".join(f"`{b}`" for b in PB[n]) for n in PB)
      + " (`forward_kwargs.prediction_boundaries`). How to read "
      "this: a condition with no field is a wall or a free surface whose identity is its own input layer; \"first wins\" is the "
      "priority where two labels mark one cell. The table does not show the global inputs or the outputs (@tbl-using-configs).")
```

```{python}
#| label: para-using-splits
#| output: asis
T2 = ISLA_CFGS["isla_tensile2d"]["dataset_append_transforms"][0]["labels"]
LUG = ISLA_CFGS["isla_lug"]["dataset_append_transforms"][0]["labels"]
AZ = ISLA_CFGS["isla_volume_aerozoo"]
assert list(T2).index("fixed") < list(T2).index("pinned") and list(LUG).index("loaded") < list(LUG).index("hole")
print(f"The label order matters where two labels mark one cell. On Tensile2d the order is {', '.join(f'`{k}`' for k in T2)}: "
      "the bottom edge's cell at the pinned corner node stays `fixed`, so the bottom edge's prescribed displacement holds "
      "along all of it, and the pinned node is marked by the left side's cell at it, which only `bc_pinned` labels. On the lug "
      f"the order is {', '.join(f'`{k}`' for k in LUG)}, because the loaded cells are part of the hole. On DeepJEB++ the "
      "split also permutes the scored cell centroids into the order of ISLA's surface predictions (the conditions in sorted "
      "order, each its cells in mesh order), the same points with the same targets. AeroZoo needs no split; its "
      "configuration instead removes dataset steps ISLA does not read (`dataset_drop_transforms`: "
      + ", ".join(f"`{t}`" for t in AZ["dataset_drop_transforms"])
      + ") and lifts the reader's per-boundary cell cap (`dataset_reader_overrides`), so the four boundaries arrive whole "
      "and the model draws their tokens.")
```

The Tensile2d configuration, as it stands in its file (comments omitted):

```{python}
#| label: code-using-tensile2d
#| output: asis
T2C = ISLA_CFGS["isla_tensile2d"]
show = {"dataset_append_transforms": T2C["dataset_append_transforms"],
        "forward_kwargs": {"boundary_meshes": T2C["forward_kwargs"]["boundary_meshes"]},
        "model": {"boundary_schemas": T2C["model"]["boundary_schemas"], "dim": T2C["model"]["dim"],
                  "interior": T2C["model"]["interior"]}}
print("```yaml\n" + yaml.safe_dump(show, sort_keys=False, default_flow_style=None).rstrip() + "\n```")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Nested field names"}
A dataset that stores its fields in groups (`solution/pressure` on disk,
`solution.pressure` in a configuration) names its targets with a dot, and
the model's `output_schema` uses the same dotted names. A dotted name or a
nested mapping spells a group: `{"solution.pressure": {"rank": 0},
"solution.velocity": {"rank": 1}}` and `{"solution": {"pressure": {"rank":
0}, "velocity": {"rank": 1}}}` declare the same model. The returned mesh's
`point_data` is nested the same way, so `out.point_data["solution",
"pressure"]` and `out.point_data["solution"]["pressure"]` address the same
leaf. The same dotted names address the fields in the meshes' `cell_data`
and `point_data` and in `global_data`.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Problems other than external aerodynamics"}
The architecture knows only that it was given named fields of declared
rank. A buoyant flow passes gravity as its one direction. A magnetized flow
passes two. Steady conduction with pinned temperatures passes no direction
and declares two conditions: the pinned boundary with its prescribed
temperature (`pinned: {trace: {rank: 0}}`) and the insulated boundary with
none (`insulated: {}`).
An elasticity problem declares its clamped boundary, its loaded boundary
with the traction as a rank-1 field, and its free surface, and predicts the
stress as one symmetric rank-2
output (`stress: {rank: 2, symmetric: true}`), from which the recipe reads
a `symmetric_tensor` target's components along the dataset's axes. Each global
direction adds one seed cosine, one relational cosine and two vectors to
the output basis; each rank-1 boundary input adds its frame cosines and
norm to its condition's seed and, through the condition's vector map, its
contraction with each anchor direction (@sec-arch-seed,
@sec-arch-layer). The tests in `test_isla_global_inputs.py`,
`test_isla_inputs.py`, `test_isla_conditions.py`, `test_isla_heads.py` and
`test_isla_nd.py` cover zero and two directions, global scalars, rank-1 and
rank-2 inputs on one condition or several, every output rank and parity,
and two dimensions.
:::

## Training {#sec-using-train}

**Train with the recipe and the ISLA model configuration of your dataset;
it pins the reference configuration, the rate and the compile options, and
ISLA needs no augmentation.** From the recipe root
(`examples/cfd/external_aerodynamics/unified_external_aero_recipe`):

```bash
# DrivAerML Surface task (sampling_resolution defaults to 200,000 cells per case).
python src/train.py model=isla_surface dataset=drivaer_ml_surface

# DrivAerML Volume task: boundary -> interior, read-only prediction points (ISLA-DTT), compiled block by block. The
# dataset file reads the vehicle and the tunnel's four pieces whole and reverses the vehicle into the fluid; the model
# draws its 200,000 boundary tokens from the five.
python src/train.py model=isla_volume dataset=drivaer_ml_volume_reference

# The same interior task with interacting prediction points (interacting ISLA), compiled whole.
python src/train.py model=isla_volume dataset=drivaer_ml_volume_reference \
    model.query_independent=false compile=true model.compile_blocks=false

# HiLiftAeroML wings: five outputs (pressure, temperature, density, velocity, wall shear stress).
python src/train.py model=isla_surface_highlift dataset=highlift_surface

# AirfRANS interior task in its plane (dim 2), uniform interior draw.
python src/train.py model=isla_volume_airfrans dataset=airfrans_uvolume_2d
```

@tbl-using-configs lists every ISLA configuration the recipe ships, read
from its file. The model configuration and the dataset file are chosen
together: the dataset file writes the fields the model declares (the unit
far-field direction `U_inf_dir`, the boundary meshes under the names of
`forward_kwargs`, the Horvitz–Thompson measures of a subsampled surface,
the orientation of an interior task's boundaries).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-using-configs
#| output: asis
def decl(d):
    tag = lambda v: "".join([", velocity source" if v.get("velocity_scale") else "", f", {v['role']}" if v.get("role") else ""])
    return ", ".join(f"`{k}` ({v['rank']}{tag(v)})" for k, v in (d or {}).items()) or "none"
o = "| configuration | task | dim | outputs (rank) | global inputs (rank) | boundary inputs | compile |\n|---|---|--:|---|---|--:|---|\n"
for n, c in ISLA_CFGS.items():
    m = c["model"]
    task = ("interior, read-only" if m.get("query_independent") else "interior") if m.get("interior") else "surface"
    comp = "whole model" if c.get("compile") else ("per block" if m.get("compile_blocks") else "none")
    o += (f"| `{n}` | {task} | {m.get('dim', DEFAULTS['dim'])} | {decl(m.get('output_schema'))} | {decl(m.get('global_schema'))} "
          f"| {sum(len(s or {}) for s in (m.get('boundary_schemas') or {}).values())} | {comp} |\n")
print(o)
print(": The recipe's ISLA model configurations (`conf/model/isla_*.yaml`, a parent's `defaults` merged in), read as the page "
      "renders. Every one is the reference configuration at the same learning rate. How to read this: \"boundary inputs\" counts "
      "the declared per-cell fields; a rank-1 global input is a direction and a rank-0 one a scalar, except a velocity source, "
      "whose magnitude is the velocity scale $U$, and a global with a role, which the declared scales consume (@sec-using-scales); \"compile\" is the whole-model `torch.compile` or the per-block `compile_blocks` (every "
      "interior configuration: ISLA-DTT's boundary read breaks the whole-model graph). It does not say which dataset file each "
      "configuration was paired with in a standing; the dataset chapters do.")
```

These commands are the training half of the reporting protocol of
@sec-protocol. ISLA needs no rotation augmentation: its outputs are exactly
covariant under rigid motions of the input, so a model trained in the
dataset's native frame predicts a body in any pose (@sec-pose).

### The learning rate {#sec-using-lr}

**Train ISLA at one rate, 3.75e-4, on every dataset; the optimizer that
makes one rate meaningful across all of its weight matrices is Muon, with
AdamW for everything that is not a matrix.**

```{python}
#| label: para-using-lr
#| output: asis
print(f"Every ISLA configuration pins this rate. The recipe-wide default (`conf/train.yaml`, "
      f"{sci(TRAIN['training']['optimizer']['lr'])}) is {TRAIN['training']['optimizer']['lr'] / next(iter(lrs.values())):.0f} times ISLA's rate, and an ISLA "
      "configuration never inherits it. For another width, start from the width rule the configuration files state, "
      "$10^{-3} \\times 192 / \\mathrm{hidden}$, which gives the reference rate at width 512, and treat it as a starting rate.")
```

```{python}
#| label: para-using-optimizer
#| output: asis
torch.manual_seed(0)
REF = ISLA(output_schema={"pressure": {"rank": 0}, "wss": {"rank": 1}}, boundary_schemas={"vehicle": {}}, global_schema={"U_inf_dir": {"rank": 1}})
two = [p for p in REF.parameters() if p.ndim == 2]; rest = [p for p in REF.parameters() if p.ndim != 2]
n2, nr = sum(p.numel() for p in two), sum(p.numel() for p in rest)
print(f"The recipe builds the optimizer from the parameters' shapes (`build_muon_optimizer` in `src/utils.py`): every 2-D "
      f"parameter goes to Muon and every other to AdamW, both at the configured rate and weight decay "
      f"{BASE['training']['optimizer']['weight_decay']:g}. In the reference configuration of the DrivAerML Surface model that "
      f"is {len(two)} matrices holding {n2:,} parameters ({100 * n2 / (n2 + nr):.2f}% of the total) under Muon, and "
      f"{len(rest)} vectors and scalars holding {nr:,} (the biases, the LayerNorm scales and shifts, the routing gains and, "
      f"in an interior model, the bias of the prediction points' input layer and, with interacting points, their routing mass) under AdamW. The rate is the same for both, and the schedule "
      f"divides it by {1 / TRAIN['training']['scheduler']['gamma']:g} every {TRAIN['training']['scheduler']['step_size']} "
      f"epochs (`{TRAIN['training']['scheduler']['_target_']}`, `conf/train.yaml`).")
```

Muon is steepest descent in the spectral norm. For a weight matrix $W$
with momentum-averaged gradient $G = U \Sigma V^{\mathsf T}$, the step that
decreases the loss fastest among steps of unit spectral norm is
$-U V^{\mathsf T}$: every singular direction of the gradient moves by the
same amount, whatever its singular value. Muon computes that polar factor
approximately, with a few Newton–Schulz iterations in bfloat16, and scales
it (`adjust_lr_fn="match_rms_adamw"`) so that its root-mean-square entry
matches that of a typical AdamW step at the same rate. Two consequences
matter for ISLA. The step on a matrix has a fixed size set by the rate
alone, not by the gradient's scale, so the rate is a statement about how
far each weight matrix moves per step; one number then serves the
embedding, the routing's base prototypes, the slice and token MLPs and the head alike.
And the vectors that Muon does not take, the LayerNorm parameters and the
biases, get AdamW's per-coordinate normalization at a matched step size.
The one rate holds on every dataset because no block multiplies the
residual stream by a learned matrix: the slice sublayer reads the
normalized state, so each block adds to the stream rather than rescaling
it (@sec-isla-layer).

## Evaluation and the inference sampler {#sec-using-sampler}

**Score in float32 at the reporting protocol's 200,000 cells. If the cell
budget is fixed and smaller, draw the cells with the stratified sampler.**
Inference shares the training configuration and reads the checkpoint by
run identifier:

```bash
# sampling_resolution=200000 is the reporting protocol; the infer default is the whole mesh
python src/infer.py model=isla_surface dataset=drivaer_ml_surface \
    run_id=<the trained run_id> infer_split=val sampling_resolution=200000 precision=float32
```

```{python}
#| label: para-using-precision
#| output: asis
INFER = yaml.safe_load((RECIPE / "conf" / "infer.yaml").read_text())
PR = json.load(open(RES / "precres_2026-09-18.json"))["reduction"]; PRB, PRF = PR["bfloat16"], PR["float32"]
print(f"The recipe trains under {BASE['precision']} autocast (`conf/base.yaml`), and `conf/infer.yaml` reads the whole mesh "
      f"by default (`sampling_resolution: {INFER['sampling_resolution']:,}`), hence the two overrides. Every number in this "
      "book is a float32 inference on the final-epoch checkpoint (@sec-metrics), on the eager path or on compiled blocks "
      "that compute the same function (@tbl-protocol). A bfloat16 inference rounds the learned maps' "
      f"arithmetic. On two trained DrivAerML Surface checkpoints, the bfloat16 pressure prediction differs from the float32 one "
      f"by {PRB['scalar_vs_fp32_unrotated']['mean_over_seeds']:.1%} on average, and a rigid motion of the input moves the "
      f"bfloat16 prediction by {min(PRB['scalar_residual']['per_seed_mean']):.1%} to {max(PRB['scalar_residual']['per_seed_mean']):.1%} "
      f"(the wall-shear vector by {min(PRB['vector_residual']['per_seed_mean']):.1%} to {max(PRB['vector_residual']['per_seed_mean']):.1%}), "
      f"where in float32 it moves by {PRF['scalar_residual']['max_over_cars']:.3%} at worst (twelve validation cars per checkpoint; "
      "an ISLA at 192 wide, 256 slices, 1e-3, linear routing, raw slice reads, @sec-study-configurations; "
      "results/precres_2026-09-18.json). If your use depends on the pose or the sampling contract, infer in float32.")
```

**For inference at a fixed cell budget, draw the cells with the stratified
sampler.** Replace the dataset's `SubsampleMesh` stage with the recipe's
`StratifiedSubsampleMesh`:

```yaml
    - _target_: ${dp:StratifiedSubsampleMesh}   # in place of SubsampleMesh
      n_cells: ${sampling_resolution}
```

The stage needs more cells than the budget to draw from, so raise or
remove the reader's `subsample_n_cells` too: in `drivaer_ml_surface.yaml`
the reader already cuts each surface to `sampling_resolution` cells, and
the stage would then keep them all. The stratified sampler keeps the same
inclusion law as `SubsampleMesh` (every cell kept with probability $n/N$,
measure weight $N/n$), so nothing about the trained model or the quantity
it estimates changes. The kept cells are a *systematic* draw along the
Morton order of the cell centroids: one cell per consecutive run of $N/n$
cells, with a single random offset. The Morton order sorts the cells by
interleaved coordinate bits, a space-filling curve along which consecutive
cells are spatial neighbors. A systematic sample has the same expectation
as an independent draw for every cell-weighted integral and a lower
variance for smooth integrands, the quadrature analog of stratified
Monte Carlo. The headline comparisons of the book on the surface tasks use
the independent draw; a deployment at a reduced budget should use the
stratified draw or more cells. The interior task needs no such stage: the
model reads its boundary whole and draws its tokens itself, by systematic
sampling along a Morton order in the boundary's canonical frame, with
inclusion probabilities proportional to area (@sec-using-interior).

**On a surface task, ask for a sample that covers the whole body, even when only one region's values are wanted, and
read the region from the output.** The cells given for the prediction boundaries are ISLA's view of the body as well as the points it predicts at, as the docstring of `prediction_boundaries` states:
the slices are measure-weighted means over them, so a cell's prediction depends on the other cells sampled with it
through the quadrature error of those means, which falls as the sample grows (@sec-limits-query-independence). A
larger sample, or the mean of the predictions of several independent samples, lowers the error.

```{python}
#| label: para-using-surface-request
#| output: asis
SQR = R.load("surfqpop", "results/out/reduced.json")
SQ = [SQR[f"r090_dr_isla_seed{s}"]["fields"] for s in (42, 43)]
_rg = lambda a, b: a if a == b else f"{a} to {b}"
sq = lambda fn: " / ".join(_rg(f"{min(fn(d[f]) for d in SQ):.3f}", f"{max(fn(d[f]) for d in SQ):.3f}") for f in ("pressure", "wss"))
half = [d[f][k]["ratio"] for d in SQ for f in ("pressure", "wss") for k in ("q3_low_x", "q3_high_x")]
print(f"On the DrivAerML Surface task (the standing's two checkpoints, its {SQR['r090_dr_isla_seed42']['n_cases']} validation "
      "cars, float32), one 200,000-cell sample's own noise, the spread between two independent samples on the cells they share "
      f"divided by the square root of two, is {sq(lambda d: d['delta']['200000'] / d['err_uniform']['200000'])} of the error on "
      "pressure / wall shear. Against the scored 200,000 cells the error is "
      f"{sq(lambda d: d['err_ratio_to_200k']['800000'])} times as large at 800,000 cells and "
      f"{sq(lambda d: d['err_ratio_to_200k']['50000'])} times at 50,000, and four disjoint 50,000-cell samples that together cover "
      f"the car give {sq(lambda d: d['q2_ratio'])} times, as one 50,000-cell sample does (means over the cars). A sample of half "
      f"the car, at the same density, raises the error on that half {min(half):.0f} to {max(half):.0f} times: given part of the "
      f"body, the model has no skill on it. Data: {R.source('surfqpop', 'results/out/reduced.json')}.")
```

## Loading a trained model {#sec-using-checkpoint}

**A checkpoint stores its own constructor arguments and its version, so
loading is one call.** A saved ISLA is a PhysicsNeMo module file (`.mdlus`,
a zip archive of the weights, the arguments and the metadata) and loads
with `ISLA.from_checkpoint`; no configuration has to be repeated. The cell
below saves the example's surface model, loads it back and reads the file.

```{python}
#| label: using-checkpoint-demo
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
path = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "isla_airfoil.mdlus")
surface.save(path)
loaded = ISLA.from_checkpoint(path).double().eval()
with torch.no_grad():
    again = loaded(boundary_meshes={"airfoil": airfoil}, prediction_boundaries=["airfoil"], global_data={"freestream": freestream})
with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as z:
    meta, args = json.loads(z.read("metadata.json")), json.loads(z.read("args.json"))["__args__"]

# The same file marked as written by an earlier version, and a state dict with torch's earlier version mark.
old = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(path), "isla_airfoil_earlier.mdlus")
with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as zin, zipfile.ZipFile(old, "w") as zout:
    for item in zin.namelist():
        data = zin.read(item)
        if item == "metadata.json":
            data = json.dumps({**json.loads(data), "mdlus_file_version": "0.8.0"}).encode()
        zout.writestr(item, data)
state = surface.state_dict()
state._metadata[""]["version"] = 8   # torch's state-dict version of the module as 0.8.0 wrote it
refusals = {}
for label, call in {"`ISLA.from_checkpoint`": lambda: ISLA.from_checkpoint(old),
                    "`load_state_dict`": lambda: loaded.load_state_dict(state)}.items():
    try:
        call()
    except (IOError, RuntimeError) as err:
        refusals[label] = f"{type(err).__name__}: {err}"
```

```{python}
#| label: para-using-checkpoint
#| output: asis
same = all(torch.equal(again.point_data[k], out.point_data[k]) for k in ("cp", "tau"))
print(f"The archive holds {', '.join(f'`{n}`' for n in sorted(zipfile.ZipFile(path).namelist()))}; its metadata records "
      f"checkpoint version {meta['mdlus_file_version']}, the class's `__model_checkpoint_version__`, and `args.json` records "
      f"every constructor argument ({', '.join(f'`{k}`' for k in args)}). The loaded model's outputs are "
      f"{'bitwise equal to' if same else 'different from'} the saved model's. The `geo_kernel` attribute is not stored: a "
      "loaded model starts at `\"auto\"`.")
assert args["query_independent"] is False and args["interior"] is False   # the resolved value, stored
print()
print("**A checkpoint carries its form.** `query_independent` is stored with the value its `None` resolved to (`False` "
      "for this surface model), so an interior checkpoint loads as the form it was saved as, ISLA-DTT or interacting ISLA, "
      "whatever the class's default, and a state dict of one form is refused by a model built as the other "
      "(`test_isla_release.py`).")
```

```{python}
#| label: para-using-refusals
#| output: asis
assert len(refusals) == 2, refusals
print(f"**A checkpoint of any version other than {ISLA.__model_checkpoint_version__} is refused, on every loading path, and "
      "ISLA keeps no upgrade path.** `ISLA.from_checkpoint` compares the recorded version with the class's and names both. The paths that "
      "load weights into a built model (`Module.load`, `load_checkpoint`, the recipe's resume, `init_from` and inference, "
      "and `load_state_dict` itself) go through a pre-hook that refuses a state dict with the parameter layout of a "
      "checkpoint before 0.7.0, or with torch's state-dict version of the module other than the class's "
      f"`_version = {ISLA._version}`. The second mark tells apart a state dict of 0.7.0 to 0.11.0, whose layout is the current "
      "one but whose weights were trained on another forward: in 0.7.0 another geometry encoding of the prediction points; in 0.7.0 "
      "and 0.8.0 a length unit from the given or drawn cells' centroids alone instead of the full-resolution boundary with each "
      "cell's own second moment; in 0.9.0, the version the standings' checkpoints were trained with, the interior geometry of "
      "@sec-standing-geometry; 0.10.0 names a head-frame variant the class does not have; and 0.11.0 has tie and on-wall "
      "bands with a first-order arithmetic share and the search's arithmetic in the raw coordinates "
      "(@sec-arch-interior-geometry). The cell above marks "
      "the example's file as written by 0.8.0 and its state dict with 0.8.0's version mark; both are refused:")
print()
for label, msg in refusals.items():
    print(f"- {label}: \"{msg}\"")
print()
print("A state dict rebuilt without torch's metadata (a dict comprehension over it) carries no version mark and is checked "
      "by its layout alone.")
```

The forward call mirrors the recipe mapping. For a model trained on
DrivAerML Surface:

```python
model = ISLA.from_checkpoint("runs/<run_id>/checkpoints/<file>.mdlus").eval()
tunnel = {"inlet": inlet, "no_slip": no_slip, "outlet": outlet, "slip": slip}   # the tunnel's four pieces, whole
out = model(boundary_meshes={"vehicle": vehicle, **tunnel}, prediction_boundaries=["vehicle"],
            global_data={"U_inf_dir": g_hat})
p, tau = out.point_data["pressure"], out.point_data["wss"]      # (N,) and (N, 3), at out.points
```

`vehicle` is a `Mesh` whose cells are the sampled surface, with the
Horvitz–Thompson measures in its `_effective_measure` cell field when the
surface is subsampled, and the four tunnel meshes are the case's stored
pieces, whole; the outputs come back at the vehicle's cells. For an interior model, pass every boundary
condition's mesh at full resolution, oriented as in training, and
`prediction_points`, and read the outputs at those points; in evaluation
mode the boundary draw has its fixed start, so the prediction is
deterministic. Deploy interacting ISLA at its training point count (200,000
at the reporting protocol on DrivAerML), because an interacting point's
prediction depends on the joint request (@sec-interior-companion). The
default interior model, ISLA-DTT (`query_independent=True`), has no such
rule and is queried at any count, alone or in chunks.

## Cost {#sec-using-cost}

```{python}
#| label: para-using-cost-lede
#| output: asis
CL = {k: c for k in S.DATASETS if (c := S.cost(k, "ISLA"))}
over = [k for k, c in CL.items() if c["peak_gib"] > 80]
print(f"**In the reference configuration ISLA trains one case per GPU in under the 80 GiB it was selected under on "
      f"{len(CL) - len(over)} of the {len(CL)} dataset tasks of @tbl-isla-cost; "
      + " and ".join(f"{S.DATASETS[k].in_sentence} peaks at {CL[k]['peak_gib']:.0f} GiB" for k in over)
      + ".** Where the memory and the time of a step go, and why, is @sec-arch-cost.")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-isla-cost
#| output: asis
import re
archs = ("ISLA", "ISLA-DTT", "GeoTransolver", "Transolver")
and_ = lambda xs: ", ".join(xs[:-1]) + " and " + xs[-1] if len(xs) > 1 else "".join(xs)
# a cell's reason, from its note: the clause that names the smoke lane, without run identifiers or step counts
why = lambda c: re.sub(r" \([a-z0-9_]+\)|, \d[\d,]* steps", "", next(p for p in c["note"].split("; ") if "smoke lane" in p))
FLAGS = {"¹": lambda c: "smoke lane" in c["note"], "‡": lambda c: "in flight" in c["note"],
         "²": lambda c: c["precision"] != "bfloat16"}
marked = {f: [] for f in FLAGS}
o = ("| dataset task | " + " | ".join(archs) + " |\n|---|" + "--:|" * len(archs) + "\n")
for k in CL:
    row = {a: S.cost(k, a) for a in archs}
    marks = {a: "".join(f for f, test in FLAGS.items() if row[a] and test(row[a])) for a in archs}
    for a in archs:
        for f in marks[a]:
            marked[f].append((k, a, row[a]))
    o += f"| {S.DATASETS[k].name} | " + " | ".join(
        (f"{row[a]['n_parameters'] / 1e6:.1f}M / {row[a]['peak_gib']:.1f} / {row[a]['step_seconds']:.3f}{marks[a]}" if row[a] else "–")
        for a in archs) + " |\n"
print(o)
named = lambda f: and_([f"{S.DATASETS[k].short} {a}" for k, a, _ in marked[f]])
COST_RAW = json.load(open(S.CHAR / S.COST_FILE))
FIXED = [S.DATASETS[k].short for k in CL if "r090fix_" in CL[k]["source"]]
BEFORE = [S.DATASETS[k].short for k in CL if "before the compile fix" in CL[k]["note"]]
TIMED = [S.DATASETS[k].short for k in COST_RAW["compiled_before_fix"]]
FIXMOVE = max(abs(S.cost(k, a)["step_seconds"] / c["step_seconds"] - 1)
              for k, v in COST_RAW["compiled_before_fix"].items() for a, c in v.items())
AZ_T = next(n for n in S.aerozoo()["arms"] if n.split()[0] == "Transolver")
print(": Training footprint of the reference configurations (ISLA and ISLA-DTT width 512, 12 layers, 512 slices; GeoTransolver "
      f"width 256; Transolver width 512, 16 layers, and on AeroZoo its own configuration, {AZ_T}), per dataset task: parameters / "
      "peak device memory [GiB] as the maximum over "
      "the ranks / the median training step [s] leaving out the compile steps, one case per rank, seed means from the training "
      f"logs of the standing's lanes. {re.sub(r' \([a-z0-9_*]+\)', '', COST_RAW['note']).replace('they trained eager only for the training-path control, at', 'they train at')} "
      f"On {and_(FIXED)} the ISLA rows are the "
      "lanes trained on the compiled path with the mix-order setting, not the eagerly trained lanes behind the standing. "
      f"ISLA's lanes on {and_(BEFORE)} trained before the mix-order setting; where both were "
      f"timed, on {and_(TIMED)}, the setting moves the median step by at most {100 * FIXMOVE:.1f}%. "
      + (f"¹ {named('¹')}: " + "; ".join(sorted({why(c) for *_, c in marked["¹"]})) + ". " if marked["¹"] else "")
      + (f"‡ {named('‡')}: the lane is still training, priced on the epochs logged so far. " if marked["‡"] else "")
      + (f"² {named('²')}: trained in float32, as logged. " if marked["²"] else "")
      + "How to read this: memory is the budget the configurations were selected under (80 GiB on DrivAerML Surface); a step time "
      "is a cost on this hardware, and parameters are not a measure of capacity across architectures. ISLA-DTT's column is "
      "its standing lanes' training, which ran its read's reference implementation in one unchunked step; the class's "
      "ISLA-DTT step is @tbl-using-dtt-cost. Data: "
      f"results/char/{S.COST_FILE}.")
```

### ISLA-DTT's training step {#sec-using-dtt-cost}

```{python}
#| label: setup-using-dtt-cost
#| include: false
# DTT-FAST's table on the final heads: one GB300, the recipe's own training step (train._run_epoch, optimizer included),
# bfloat16, per-block compile, median of 15 timed steps; three columns of one job per case. Code: interacting ISLA and the
# reference ISLA-DTT at b4b10d5a9 (no fast pieces, no chunked step), ISLA-DTT at 4d281a702 (the class as merged)
F2 = R.md_table("dtt_fast_done", "final2/TABLE.md", "Main table")
F2_COL = {"isla": "interacting ISLA b4b10d5a9", "ref": "ISLA-DTT ref b4b10d5a9", "dtt": "ISLA-DTT 4d281a702"}
def f2_cell(row, col):
    """(step ms, peak GiB), or None where the step ran out of the GPU's memory."""
    c = row[F2_COL[col]]
    return None if c.startswith("OOM") else (R.num(c, 0), R.num(c, 1))
F2_ROWS = [(r_["case"], int(R.num(r_["points"])), {c: f2_cell(r_, c) for c in F2_COL}) for r_ in F2]
assert all(v["dtt"] and v["isla"] for *_, v in F2_ROWS)
# the fixed-count state (the point count never changes in the process, as in training at the registered counts), two jobs
F2S = {r_["case"]: r_ for r_ in R.md_table("dtt_fast_done", "final2/TABLE.md", "Fixed-count state")}
fx = lambda case, col: R.num(F2S[case][col], 0)
FIXED = {case: dict(dtt=sorted((fx(case, "4d281a702 fixed / varied"), fx(case, "4d281a702 repeat fixed / varied (pose job)"))),
                    isla=fx(case, "interacting b4b10d5a9 fixed / varied"), ref=fx(case, "ref b4b10d5a9 fixed / varied"),
                    n=int(R.num(F2S[case]["points"])))
         for case in F2S}
F2T = " ".join(R.load("dtt_fast_done", "final2/TABLE.md").split())
CAP = float(re.search(r"It still fits a GB300 \(([\d.]+) GiB as the rule reads it\)", F2T).group(1))
DFR = " ".join(R.load("dtt_fast_done", "FINAL_REPORT.md").split())
MAXN = re.search(r"up to ([\d.]+)M on DrivAerML", DFR).group(1)
# the same column on two nodes: the spread of its median, by setting and state
REP = {r_["run"]: R.num(r_["spread"]) for r_ in R.md_table("dtt_fast_done", "final2/TABLE.md", "Repeats of a column")}
rep = lambda pre, tags: max(v for k, v in REP.items() if k.startswith(pre) and any(g in k for g in tags))
REP_3D = rep("after_", ("drv_", "aerozoo"))
REP_AF = max(v for k, v in REP.items() if k.startswith("after_airfrans"))
REP_AF_FIXED = rep("afterS_", ("airfrans",))
REP_LUG = rep("after_", ("lug",))
```

```{python}
#| label: para-using-dtt-cost
#| output: asis
big = [(c, n, v) for c, n, v in F2_ROWS if c.startswith(("DrivAerML", "AeroZoo")) and v["ref"]]
sp = [v["ref"][0] / v["dtt"][0] for *_, v in big]; mp = [v["dtt"][1] / v["ref"][1] for *_, v in big]
drv = [(c, n, v) for c, n, v in F2_ROWS if c.startswith("DrivAerML")]
az = [(c, n, v) for c, n, v in F2_ROWS if c.startswith("AeroZoo")]
af = [(c, n, v) for c, n, v in F2_ROWS if c.startswith("AirfRANS")]
lug = next(v for c, n, v in F2_ROWS if c.startswith("lug"))
rx = lambda rows, i: [v["dtt"][i] / v["isla"][i] for *_, v in rows]
oom = [(c, n, v) for c, n, v in drv if v["ref"] is None]
w400 = next(v for c, n, v in drv if c == "DrivAerML whole boundary" and n == 400_000)
v400 = next(v for c, n, v in drv if c == "DrivAerML vehicle" and n == 400_000)
w200 = next(v for c, n, v in drv if c == "DrivAerML whole boundary" and n == 200_000)
assert {n for _, n, _ in oom} == {400_000}
rng = lambda xs, f="{:.2f}": f.format(min(xs)) + " to " + f.format(max(xs)) if f.format(min(xs)) != f.format(max(xs)) else f.format(min(xs))
print(f"**On one GB300, ISLA-DTT's training step takes {rng([1 / s for s in sp])} of the time of its read's reference "
      f"implementation in one unchunked step, at {rng(mp)} of its peak memory, on the DrivAerML Volume task and AeroZoo; it "
      f"costs {rng(rx(drv, 0))} times interacting ISLA's step on the DrivAerML Volume task and {rng(rx(az, 0))} times on "
      f"AeroZoo, both forms compiled block by block.** @tbl-using-dtt-cost times the recipe's own training step, optimizer included, of the three in one job per "
      "case (@sec-arch-tree-exec for the pieces). At 400,000 prediction points on the DrivAerML Volume task the reference "
      f"implementation runs out of the GPU's memory, and ISLA-DTT takes {v400['dtt'][0]:,.0f} ms with the vehicle and "
      f"{w400['dtt'][0]:,.0f} ms with the whole boundary; a chunked training step has run at up to {MAXN} million prediction "
      "points per case on DrivAerML.")
print()
dw, za, ra = (FIXED[k] for k in ("DrivAerML whole boundary", "AeroZoo", "AirfRANS whole boundary"))
print("**At the point counts the recipe's configurations train at, where the count never changes within a process, "
      "ISLA-DTT's step is "
      f"{dw['dtt'][0]:,.0f} to {dw['dtt'][1]:,.0f} ms on the DrivAerML Volume task with the whole boundary at {dw['n']:,} "
      f"prediction points, {za['dtt'][0]:,.0f} to {za['dtt'][1]:,.0f} ms on AeroZoo at {za['n']:,} and {ra['dtt'][0]:,.0f} to "
      f"{ra['dtt'][1]:,.0f} ms on the AirfRANS interior task with its far field at {ra['n']:,}.** Interacting ISLA takes "
      f"{dw['isla']:,.0f}, {za['isla']:,.0f} and {ra['isla']:,.0f} ms there, and the reference implementation "
      f"{dw['ref']:,.0f}, {za['ref']:,.0f} and {ra['ref']:,.0f} ms. The configurations draw a fixed `sampling_resolution`, "
      "and the two numbers of each range come from two jobs on two nodes. On "
      f"AirfRANS a process whose counts vary runs the same code up to {REP_AF:.0f}% apart from one "
      f"process to the next, against {REP_AF_FIXED:.1f}% at a fixed count, so its rows in @tbl-using-dtt-cost carry that "
      "spread.")
print()
print(f"**ISLA-DTT's peak is that of one chunk of every point, because the size rule takes the fewest chunks that fit, "
      f"and here one chunk fits.** At these counts every point of a case runs in one chunk: {w200['dtt'][1]:.0f} GiB at 200,000 points on "
      f"the DrivAerML Volume task with the whole boundary, on a card the rule reads as {CAP:.0f} GiB. A step cut into more "
      "chunks holds less memory and takes longer, so a peak here measures what one chunk of every point needs, not the "
      f"least the step can run in. On the GINOT bracket lug, all {next(n for c, n, v in F2_ROWS if c.startswith('lug')):,} "
      f"nodes of one case, ISLA-DTT's step is {lug['dtt'][0]:.0f} ms against interacting ISLA's {lug['isla'][0]:.0f} ms.")
```

```{python}
    GEO_COST[k] = dict(geo_base=P0[k][0], step_base=P0[k][1], geo_unfused=g[0], geo_fast=g[1], geo_ref=g[2],
                       step_unfused=s[0], step_fast=s[1], step_ref=s[2])
```
