```{python}
assert all(r["kernel"] == "fast" for r in GT_ if r["arm"].startswith("head"))   # auto resolved to the fast search
NPASS = {a: {len(nums(r["geometry call per pass (ms)"])) for r in GT_ if r["arm"].startswith(a)} for a in ("head", "reference")}
assert NPASS == {"head": {3}, "reference": {2}}
GEO_PEAK = {}
for r in GT_:
    GEO_PEAK.setdefault(r["case"], []).append(float(r["peak GiB"]))
assert len(GEO_PEAK) == len(GEO_COST)
assert all(max(v) == min(v) for v in GEO_PEAK.values())   # the same peak in every arm of a case
# the class's reference arm as GEO-BAND's phase 0 timed it, without the derived bands, against this table's
P0R = {r["case (Q / F)"]: (nums(r["geometry call: base / reference / fast [ms]"])[1], nums(r["step: base / reference / fast [ms]"])[1])
       for r in R.md_table("geo_band_phase0", "PHASE0.md", "The book's 06 cost table")}
dref = lambda i, col: [100 * (1 - P0R[k][i] / c[col]) for k, c in GEO_COST.items()]
PH0 = " ".join(R.load("geo_band_phase0", "PHASE0.md").split())
assert "The base column agrees between the two jobs within 1-3 % on every case" in PH0

     "step: 0.9.0 / the class, reference / the class, auto [ms] | step ratio to 0.9.0: reference / auto |\n|---|--:|--:|--:|\n")
for k, c in GEO_COST.items():
    o += (f"| {k} | {c['geo_base']:,.1f} / {c['geo_ref']:,.1f} / {c['geo_fast']:,.1f} | "
          f"{c['step_base']:,.0f} / {c['step_ref']:,.0f} / {c['step_fast']:,.0f} | "
          f"{c['step_ref'] / c['step_base']:.2f} / {c['step_fast'] / c['step_base']:.2f} |\n")
print(o)
print(": The cost of ISLA's interior geometry in training: the geometry call and the training step with the geometry the "
      "standings' checkpoints trained with (0.9.0, @sec-standing-geometry) and with the class's, its bounds for thin cells "
      "and derived bands included (@sec-arch-interior-geometry), under its two search kernels: *reference*, which runs "
      "wherever the model runs, and *auto*, the default, which takes the fast search on CUDA where Triton imports (as here) "
      "and the reference search elsewhere. The same recipe, settings and network otherwise. One GB300, bfloat16, eager, one "
      "case per step, the GPUs rotated between passes; each pass gives the median after five warm-up calls or steps, and "
      "each cell of the class's columns is the mean of its passes' medians (the reference two, auto three). The 0.9.0 "
      "column comes from another job of the same protocol on another node, the mean of two passes; its 0.9.0 timings agree "
      "within 1 to 3% with those of a third job on every case. The class's reference arm, timed in that other job without the "
      f"derived bands, reads {min(dref(0, 'geo_ref')):.0f} to {max(dref(0, 'geo_ref')):.0f}% shorter per geometry call and "
      f"{min(dref(1, 'step_ref')):.0f} to {max(dref(1, 'step_ref')):.0f}% shorter per step than here, so a step ratio to "
      "0.9.0 carries a few percent of spread between jobs. *Step ratio*: the class's step ÷ the 0.9.0 step. How to read "
      "this: the whole-boundary row reads the DrivAerML tunnel box beside the vehicle; there 0.9.0's geometry seeded its "
      "search with a query that cost about two seconds, which the class's cell-tree seed does not have. In two dimensions "
      "both kernels run the same search over the segments. Peak memory of the training process is the same, to the 0.1 GiB "

      f"{R.source('geo_thinfast', 'lhr/timing_table.md')}; the 0.9.0 column, {R.source('geo_band_phase0', 'PHASE0.md')}. "
```

```{python}
whole = next(c for k, c in GEO_COST.items() if "whole" in k)
vk = next(k for k in GEO_COST if "vehicle" in k)
r_f = {k: c["step_fast"] / c["step_base"] for k, c in body3.items()}
r_r = {k: c["step_ref"] / c["step_base"] for k, c in body3.items()}
faster3 = {k: 1 - c["geo_fast"] / c["geo_ref"] for k, c in GEO_COST.items() if not k.startswith("AirfRANS")}
assert min(faster3.values()) > 0
most = max(faster3, key=faster3.get).split(" (")[0]
print(f"**The exact interior geometry adds {100 * (min(r_f.values()) - 1):.0f} to {100 * (max(r_f.values()) - 1):.0f}% to a "
      "training step on a three-dimensional body alone under the default search, and nothing measurable in two dimensions** "
      f"(@tbl-using-geometry-cost; on AirfRANS {af['step_fast'] / af['step_base']:.2f} times the standings' step). The geometry "
      "call computes every candidate distance in float64, every tie set and least-norm direction, and the winding number at "
      f"every prediction point; on the DrivAerML Volume case with the vehicle alone that call is "
      f"{GEO_COST[vk]['geo_fast'] / GEO_COST[vk]['geo_base']:.1f} times the standings' geometry call. The default, "
      '`geometry_kernel="auto"`, takes the fast search on CUDA where Triton imports, which returns the same geometry '
      f"bitwise and cuts the geometry call by {100 * min(faster3.values()):.0f} to {100 * max(faster3.values()):.0f}% on every "
      f"three-dimensional case, the most on the {most}: it lowers the geometry's cost and does not remove it. It is optional, "
      "as Peter's ruling on the geometry's cost asks: "
      '"If the speedup experiment works, then add an optional fast path (like our other kernels, where we default iff '

      f"CPU, the reference search runs; on the GB300 it makes a three-dimensional step cost {100 * (min(r_r.values()) - 1):.0f} to "
      f"{100 * (max(r_r.values()) - 1):.0f}% more than the standings' (the reference column). To force one search, set "
      '`geometry_kernel` to `"reference"` or `"fast"`; checkpoints do not store it. With the DrivAerML tunnel box read '

assert "(+" not in CH["AirfRANS 2-D"][REFC] + CH["AirfRANS 2-D"][FASTC]
```

```{python}
MIS = [("the DrivAerML Surface task", ex("DrivAerML Surface", "whole")), ("AirfRANS", ex("AirfRANS", "airfoil + freestream")),
       ("the lug", ex("lug", "surface")), ("Tensile2d", ex("Tensile2d", "outer")), ("DeepJEB++", ex("DeepJEB++", "surface"))]
assert ex("DrivAerML Volume", "whole") == 0 and all(ex("AeroZoo", v) == 0 for v in ("4 boundaries (azc full",))
from physicsnemo.experimental.models.isla.model import TOKEN_ALIGNMENT
# MERGE-PREP's interleaved GB300 timing of the padding (job 366130): GPU time per training step, padded ÷ unpadded code
TM = R.md_table("boundary_merge", "results/TIMING.md")
gpu = lambda case: [R.num(r["GPU ms / step, fix / base"]) for r in TM if r["case, mode"].startswith(case) and r["N (mod 32)"].startswith("natural")]
pad_cut = [1 - g for c in ("lug", "Tensile2d") for g in gpu(c)]
same = [R.num(r["GPU ms / step, fix / base"]) for r in TM if r["case, mode"].endswith("eager") and r["N (mod 32)"].startswith("aligned")]
assert len(pad_cut) == 4 and max(abs(s - 1) for s in same) < 0.0015
print(f"**ISLA pads its token axis to a multiple of {TOKEN_ALIGNMENT}, because a token count that is not one trains "
      "slower.** Unpadded, in bfloat16 on a GB300, on the DrivAerML Surface task and "
      f"AeroZoo, a step at an odd token count takes {min(odd):.2f} to {max(odd):.2f} times as long as at the same count padded to "
      f"a multiple of 32, and at an even count that is not a multiple of 8, {min(even):.2f} to {max(even):.2f} times, eager and "
      "with the blocks compiled alike. The time goes to the slice attention's matrix products along the token axis, whose fast "
      "kernels need a token stride of 16 bytes, and to LayerNorm's backward pass, whose weight-gradient reduction over more "
      "than 65,536 rows takes its fast path only at a multiple of 32 rows. The count is the boundary tokens and prediction points of a case, fixed per case. So "
      f"`_forward_tokens` completes the token set to a multiple of `TOKEN_ALIGNMENT` = {TOKEN_ALIGNMENT} with tokens whose fields "
      "are zero and whose log measure is $-\\infty$: they hold no measure in any softmax over points, so no other token reads "
      "them, and no output is read from them, so outputs and gradients are the unpadded ones up to the summation order of the "
      "longer reductions. Where nothing is padded, the eager forward runs no padding at all and its outputs and gradients are "
      "bitwise those of the unpadded code. The pad runs on " + ", ".join(f"{100 * f:.0f}% of the training cases of {n}" for n, f in MIS[:-1])
      + f" and {100 * MIS[-1][1]:.0f}% of {MIS[-1][0]}, and on none of AeroZoo's or the DrivAerML Volume task's. Where it "
      f"pads, on a case of the lug and of Tensile2d, a training step takes {100 * min(pad_cut):.0f} to {100 * max(pad_cut):.0f}% "
      "less GPU time than unpadded, eager and with the blocks compiled (one GB300, bfloat16, interleaved runs). Under the "
      "whole-model compile the pad always runs, since a test for an empty pad would guard the dynamic count; that path's step "
      "time was not measured, and its compile tests pass on a GB300. Data: "
      f"{R.source('align8', 'results/repro_table.md')}; {R.source('align8', 'exposure/exposure_classes.tsv')}; "
      f"{R.source('boundary_merge', 'results/TIMING.md')}; {R.source('boundary_merge', 'REPORT.md')} (part 1).")
```

```{python}
      f"direction, the global directions and the shared boundary vector channels number at most {GK.MAX_DIRECTIONS}, there are at most "
      f"{GK.MAX_SLICES:,} slices and no rank-2 per-token input; otherwise it runs the eager region, which computes the same "
      "function. It logs the choice once. A planar model, a model with no global direction (the lug) and a model with "

      "before the first forward pass.")
print("- **So are ISLA-DTT's tree-read kernels.** Under the default `tree_read_kernel=\"auto\"` the forest build and the walk "
      "run their Warp kernels on CUDA (Warp, like Triton, is a Python framework for writing GPU kernels) and the read its fused "
      "Triton kernel on CUDA outside float64, each where its own requirements hold, and each logs its choice once; on the CPU "
      "every piece runs its reference, and in float64 the read does. All of them compute the same forest, the same pairs and "
      "the same read up to summation order (@sec-arch-tree-exec). Set `\"reference\"` to run every reference. The recipe "
      "trains ISLA-DTT in the fewest chunks of prediction points that fit the GPU, chosen before any point's forward pass and "
      "bounded alike on every rank (@sec-using-dtt-cost).")

assert all(c.get("compile_options") == opts for c in ISLA_CFGS.values())   # one set of options in every configuration
yv = lambda v: str(v).lower() if isinstance(v, bool) else v
_ind = opts["options"]   # Inductor's options
assert _ind == {"max_autotune": True, "coordinate_descent_tuning": True, "triton.mix_order_reduction": False}
assert all(ISLA_CFGS[n]["model"].get("interior") for n in _rest) and not any(ISLA_CFGS[n]["model"].get("interior") for n in _whole)
print(f"- **Compile the whole model on the surface task.** The recipe's surface configurations do ({', '.join(f'`{n}`' for n in _whole)}): "
      "`compile: true` with `compile_options` "
      + ", ".join(f"`{k}: {yv(v)}`" for k, v in opts.items() if k != "options")
      + " and the Inductor `options` " + ", ".join(f"`{k}: {yv(v)}`" for k, v in _ind.items())
      + ", the same options in every configuration. The first two Inductor options are those of the mode "
      "`max-autotune-no-cudagraphs`, written out so that the third can turn off Inductor's mix-order reduction, a fusion of a "
      "per-point sum with a sum over the points: torch 2.12 returns that sum at the wrong rank on the AirfRANS graph, and torch 2.12 "
      "and 2.13 add padded rows to its column sums (pytorch/pytorch#195845; the comment in `isla_volume_airfrans.yaml`). The "
      "block-by-block compile below sets the same option itself (`_BLOCK_COMPILE_OPTIONS` in `model.py`: "
      + ", ".join(f"`{k}: {yv(v)}`" for k, v in IM._BLOCK_COMPILE_OPTIONS.items()) + "). The forward, `Mesh` in and out, "
      "traces to one graph and compiles once with dynamic shapes, so the case-to-case "
      "change in mesh size does not recompile; validation, in eval mode, compiles a second graph. The first compile is "
      "long, so keep `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` and `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` across the links of a chained run. The options leave "
      "out CUDA graphs on purpose: they are static-shape and would record a graph for every case size.")
P3 = json.load(open(RES / "perf3_neutrality_2026-10-01.json"))
rat = {ds: P3["datasets"][ds]["ratio"] for ds in ("drivaerml_surface", "drivaerml_volume") if ds in P3["datasets"]}
lo = min(v for r in rat.values() for v in r.values()); hi = max(v for r in rat.values() for v in r.values())
LUGT = R.md_table("ref090", "r090_final_tables.md", "REF-090-FIX GINOT lug")[0]
lug_t = R.num(LUGT["T = retrained ÷ original (s42, s43 paired)"])
print(f"- **Compile block by block where the whole graph breaks.** `compile_blocks: true` runs each slice block's forward "
      "under `torch.compile` instead, with parameter names, the state dict and the eager path unchanged. It is the way to "
      "compile ISLA-DTT, whose boundary read breaks the whole-model graph, and every interior configuration uses it "
      f"({', '.join(f'`{n}`' for n in _rest)}: `compile: false`, `compile_blocks: true`); interacting ISLA on AeroZoo needs "
      "it too, since that dataset's four boundaries recompile the whole graph. The standing's "
      "training runs use it on every dataset but Tensile2d, AirfRANS and the lug, whose ISLA standings train eagerly (@tbl-protocol). On the DrivAerML tasks, whose geometry runs in the "
      f"fused kernel, models trained with it score as models trained eagerly do: compiled ÷ eager error between {lo:.3f} and "
      f"{hi:.3f} on every field, seed means of two seeds (results/perf3_neutrality_2026-10-01.json). Without the mix-order "
      "setting, under torch 2.12, the compiled blocks compute another function on AirfRANS, Tensile2d and the lug, whose "
      "geometry runs in the eager region, and on the lug that changed what training found: retrained with the setting, "
      f"ISLA's von Mises error is {lug_t:.3f} times that of the same run without it, both scored eagerly "
      f"({R.source('ref090', 'r090_final_tables.md')}). With the setting, block by block against eager on trained ISLA-DTT "
      "checkpoints, the compiled blocks agree to 1.5e-5 relative in float32 and at roundoff in float64; in bfloat16 they "
      "round fewer intermediates than eager does: each block's output is no farther from float64 than eager's, and the "
      "model's outputs and parameter gradients are 1.0 to 1.4 times eager's distance to float64 "
      f"({R.source('dtt_fast_compile', 'RESULTS.md')}). Whether they meet the supervisor's certification policy for "
      "compiled regions, which compares each tensor group with eager's own change under a one-ulp perturbation of its "
      "inputs, is not measured (@sec-arch-cost).")
```

## Contracts you can check on your own data {#sec-using-contracts}

**Each contract is a few lines on a loaded model, and a residual far above
roundoff points at the inputs, not the model.** The contracts are exact
properties of the code (@sec-isla-contracts). The cell below runs five of
them on the example's surface model in float64: a rotation with a
translation, a reflection, a uniform rescale of the geometry, a rescale of
the measures alone, and every cell split into two coincident copies of half
its measure, which re-represents the same boundary. Scalars must be
unchanged and vectors must rotate with the body.

```{python}
#| label: using-contracts-demo
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
def run(mesh, g):
    with torch.no_grad():
        o = surface(boundary_meshes={"airfoil": mesh}, prediction_boundaries=["airfoil"], global_data={"freestream": g})
    return o.point_data["cp"], o.point_data["tau"]

rel = lambda a, b: float((a - b).norm() / b.norm())
f64 = dict(dtype=torch.float64)
cos_, sin_ = math.cos(0.7), math.sin(0.7)
R = torch.tensor([[cos_, -sin_], [sin_, cos_]], **f64)  # a rotation by 0.7 rad
F = torch.tensor([[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, -1.0]], **f64)    # a reflection across the x-axis
t = torch.tensor([3.0, -2.0], **f64)                  # a translation
w = airfoil.cell_areas                                # the segment lengths
checks = {  # name: (transformed boundary, transformed direction, map of the vectors)
    "rotation by 0.7 rad and translation by (3, -2)":
        (Mesh(points=verts @ R.T + t, cells=cells), freestream @ R.T, R),
    "reflection across the x-axis (cells reversed to keep normals outward)":
        (Mesh(points=verts @ F.T, cells=cells.flip(1)), freestream @ F.T, F),
    "geometry scaled by 7 (measures scale with it)":
        (Mesh(points=7.0 * verts, cells=cells), freestream, None),
    "measures scaled by 5, geometry unchanged":
        (Mesh(points=verts, cells=cells, cell_data={"_effective_measure": 5.0 * w}),
         freestream, None),
    "every cell split into two coincident halves":
        (Mesh(points=verts, cells=torch.cat([cells, cells]),
              cell_data={"_effective_measure": torch.cat([w, w]) / 2}), freestream, None),
}
cp0, tau0 = run(airfoil, freestream)
residuals = {}
for name, (mesh, g, Q) in checks.items():
    cp, tau = run(mesh, g)
    cp, tau = cp[:len(cp0)], tau[:len(tau0)]          # the split mesh returns each token twice
    residuals[name] = (rel(cp, cp0), rel(tau, tau0 if Q is None else tau0 @ Q.T))
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-using-contracts
#| output: asis
o = "| transformation of the input | scalar output: relative change | vector output: relative change from the transformed prediction |\n|:----------|--:|--:|\n"
for name, (a, b) in residuals.items():
    e = lambda x: "0 (bitwise)" if x == 0 else f"{x:.1e}"
    o += f"| {name} | {e(a)} | {e(b)} |\n"
print(o)
print(f": Contract residuals of the example's untrained surface model in float64, computed as the page renders (unit roundoff "
      f"{torch.finfo(torch.float64).eps / 2:.1e}). How to read this: each entry is the relative L2 norm of the difference between "
      "the model's output on the transformed input and the transformed output on the original input; zero to roundoff is the "
      "contract. A trained checkpoint meets the same contracts, at float32 roundoff in float32. The table does not test an "
      "interior model, whose prediction points must be transformed with the boundary.")
```

On a trained checkpoint and your own data, run the same comparisons in
float32. A residual far above float32 roundoff points at the inputs:
cells with inconsistent orientation, effective measures that change with
the pose (a rigid motion leaves each cell's measure unchanged), or positions that were centered or scaled by a
sample-dependent quantity before the model saw them. The model normalizes
the normals and the global directions itself, so their magnitudes cannot
cause a residual. For an interior model, transform the prediction points
with the boundary; the default read-only model (ISLA-DTT) can also be checked for
query independence by predicting at a subset of the points and comparing
with the full request.
